data.name: Usage
data.value: Usage: marquee devices marquee show-image <file> [--orientation portrait|portrait-flipped|landscape|landscape-flipped] [--brightness 0-100] [--repeat N] [--sink <folder>] marquee sensors [--sensors lhm|hwinfo|none] [--no-claude-usage] [--raw] [--config <file>] marquee run [<theme-folder>] [--orientation ...] [--fps 1-60] [--sensors lhm|hwinfo|none] [--preview] [--sink <folder>] [--frames N] [--http-port 1024-65535 | --no-http] [--no-claude-usage] [--no-fps] [--config <file>] marquee validate <theme-folder|zip> [--fps 1-60] marquee edit [<theme-folder>] (opens the theme editor; with no theme, on the one config.yaml names) marquee push <key> <value> [--ttl 30s|5m|2h] [--port 1024-65535] [--config <file>] marquee setup-claude [--undo] [--dry-run] marquee task install [--tray <file>] | remove [--updates] | status | start [--user <SID>] | stop marquee claim-screen (in an administrator terminal: stops L-Connect until a running Marquee has the screen) marquee statusline (Claude Code runs this; see setup-claude) Settings not given on the command line come from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Marquee\config.yaml, or the file --config names. A --sink run reads only the file --config names, and leaves the saved Claude Code limits alone.
data.comment: Printed when the arguments are wrong. Commands, options and paths stay as they are; names such as <file>, the note in parentheses and the last two sentences may be translated.

data.name: LogWarning
data.value: Warning: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the warning.

data.name: LogError
data.value: Error: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the error.

data.name: NoSupportedScreens
data.value: No supported screens found.
data.comment: marquee devices, with no screen plugged in.

data.name: NoScreenFound
data.value: No supported screen found. Run `marquee devices` to check.

data.name: CouldNotReadImage
data.value: Could not read image: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the image file.

data.name: ImageStretchedToPortrait
data.value: Warning: image is {0}x{1} but the portrait canvas is {2}x{3}; it will be stretched.
data.comment: {0}x{1} is the image's width and height in pixels, {2}x{3} the screen's.

data.name: ImageStretchedToLandscape
data.value: Warning: image is {0}x{1} but the landscape canvas is {2}x{3}; it will be stretched.
data.comment: {0}x{1} is the image's width and height in pixels, {2}x{3} the screen's.

data.name: SentImage
data.value: Sent {0} to {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the image file, {1} the screen's name.

data.name: SentImageWithFirmware
data.value: Sent {0} to {1} (firmware {2}).
data.comment: {0} is the image file, {1} the screen's name, {2} its firmware version.

data.name: PushedFrames
data.value: Pushed {0} frames, average {1:F1} ms per frame
data.comment: {0} is how many frames, {1:F1} the average milliseconds per frame.

data.name: SourceFailed
data.value: {0} failed: {1}
data.comment: {0} is a sensor source, {1} the reason.

data.name: NoReadings
data.value: No provider returned any readings.

data.name: RawReadings
data.value: Raw readings from {0}:
data.comment: marquee sensors --raw, above the list of the hardware source's own readings. {0} is the source, such as "Hardware sensors (HWiNFO)".

data.name: NoRawReadings
data.value: There is no hardware source (sensors: none), so --raw has no readings to list.
data.comment: marquee sensors --raw with no hardware source. --raw and "sensors: none" stay as they are.

data.name: ConfigFileMissing
data.value: There is no {0}; using the default settings.
data.comment: {0} is the config file --config names, as a full path.

data.name: DataFolderUnusable
data.value: Marquee is running as administrator, so it keeps its log and the Claude Code limits in a folder only administrators can change, and that folder can't be used. {0}
data.comment: Printed when marquee run, elevated, can't use its folder under %ProgramData%\Marquee, and stops. {0} says which folder and why, and what to do, in English.

data.name: TrayHoldsScreen
data.value: Marquee's tray app is showing the screen; pause it from the tray (or quit it) to use marquee run.
data.comment: Printed when marquee run is started while the tray app (MarqueeTray.exe) is showing the screen, and run stops. "marquee run" stays as it is.

data.name: SinkNeedsTheme
data.value: A --sink run reads no config.yaml unless --config names one, so pass a theme folder to marquee run.
data.comment: Printed when marquee run --sink is given no theme folder and no --config, and run stops. "--sink", "config.yaml", "--config" and "marquee run" stay as they are.

data.name: SettingsUnchanged
data.value: {0} (the current settings stay until the file is fixed)
data.comment: Logged when config.yaml changes while marquee run is going but can't be used. {0} is the error, starting with its line number where there is one.

data.name: FramesNotDelivered
data.value: only {0} of {1} frame(s) reached {2}.
data.comment: Follows "Error: ". {0} is how many frames arrived, {1} how many were asked for, {2} the screen's name.

data.name: RenderedFrames
data.value: Rendered {0} frame(s) to {1}.
data.comment: {0} is how many frames, {1} the screen's name.

data.name: RenderingTo
data.value: Rendering to {0}. Edit the theme and save to reload; press Ctrl+C to stop.
data.comment: {0} is the screen's name.

data.name: RenderStatus
data.value: {0:0.0} fps (target {1}) · render {2:0.0} ms · send {3:0.0} ms · {4} frames sent
data.comment: Shown each second in the preview. {0:0.0} is the frame rate, {1} the target rate, {2:0.0} and {3:0.0} milliseconds per frame to render and to send, {4} the frames sent so far.

data.name: InvalidCustomKey
data.value: '{0}' is not a valid key: use letters, digits, _ and dots after "custom." ({1} characters at most).
data.comment: {0} is the key as typed, {1} the longest a key may be. "custom." is part of every key and stays as it is.

data.name: HttpOffInConfig
data.value: Custom values are turned off in {0} (http: off), so Marquee isn't listening for them. Turn http on there, or pass --port if Marquee was started with --http-port.
data.comment: marquee push without --port. {0} is the path of config.yaml. "http: off" and "http" are what the file says and stay as they are.

data.name: UnknownProgram
data.value: an unknown program
data.comment: Fills {0} in RunSetupFromMarquee when Windows doesn't say which program is running.

data.name: RunSetupFromMarquee
data.value: Run setup-claude from marquee.exe itself (this is {0}), so Claude Code gets a command that works on its own.
data.comment: {0} is the program that ran setup-claude, a path or UnknownProgram.

data.name: DryRunWouldWrite
data.value: Dry run: nothing was written. {0} would become:
data.comment: {0} is the path of Claude Code's settings file; its new contents follow on the next lines.

data.name: WithoutDryRun
data.value: Without --dry-run: {0}
data.comment: {0} says what setup-claude would change.

data.name: LimitsAppearAfterSetup
data.value: Limits appear once `marquee run` is going and a Claude Code session updates its status line. A project's .claude/settings.json or managed settings with their own statusLine take precedence over this one.

data.name: CouldNotUpdateClaudeSettings
data.value: Could not update Claude Code's settings: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason.

data.name: ValidateErrorOnLine
data.comment: marquee validate, one problem. {0} is a file in the theme (layout.yaml, say), {1} the line, {2} the problem (English). Editors and scripts read "file:line:", so keep that part as it is.

data.name: ValidateError
data.comment: marquee validate, a problem not on one line. {0} is a file in the theme, or the theme's path for the theme as a whole; {1} the problem (English).

data.name: ValidateWarningOnLine
data.comment: As ValidateErrorOnLine, for something that works but may not be what the author meant.

data.name: ValidateWarning
data.value: {0}: warning: {1}
data.comment: As ValidateError, for something that works but may not be what the author meant.

data.name: ValidateSummary
data.comment: marquee validate's last line. {0} is the theme's name, {1} its orientation as layout.yaml says it (landscape or portrait, which stay as they are), {2}×{3} its width and height in pixels, {4} NoProblemsFound or the counts.

data.name: ValidateSummaryNoCanvas
data.comment: As ValidateSummary, for a theme whose layout.yaml declares no valid canvas.

data.name: ValidateZipElevated
data.value: Marquee is running as administrator, so it won't check a .zip: it would unpack it into your temp folder, which your other programs can change. Run marquee validate on the .zip from a normal terminal, or unzip it and validate the folder.
data.comment: marquee validate, run as administrator on a .zip, checked nothing. The command name stays as it is.

data.name: NoProblemsFound
data.value: no problems found
data.comment: Fills {4} in ValidateSummary.

data.name: OneError
data.value: 1 error

data.name: ManyErrors
data.value: {0} errors
data.comment: {0} is how many, 2 or more.

data.name: OneWarning
data.value: 1 warning

data.name: ManyWarnings
data.value: {0} warnings
data.comment: {0} is how many, 2 or more.

data.name: ErrorsAndWarnings
data.comment: {0} is OneError or ManyErrors, {1} OneWarning or ManyWarnings.

data.name: TaskNeedsAdministrator
data.value: `{0}` needs an administrator terminal, because the logon task runs with administrator rights. Open Terminal or PowerShell with "Run as administrator" and run it again.
data.comment: {0} is the command, such as `marquee task install`, which stays as it is. "Run as administrator" is Windows' own menu item: use its name in the user's language.

data.name: TrayNotFound
data.value: The tray app {0} does not exist. Install Marquee, which puts it next to marquee.exe, or give its path with --tray.
data.comment: {0} is the path of MarqueeTray.exe. "--tray" is an option and stays as it is.

data.name: TrayNotInProgramFiles
data.value: {0} is not under Program Files, so the logon task was not installed. The task starts the tray with administrator rights at every logon, so anyone who can change that file would get them. Install Marquee with its installer, or name a tray you trust with --tray.
data.comment: {0} is the path of MarqueeTray.exe beside marquee.exe. "Program Files" is Windows' folder: use its name in the user's language. "--tray" is an option and stays as it is.

data.name: TrayOutsideProgramFiles
data.value: Warning: {0} is not under Program Files. The logon task starts it with administrator rights, so anyone who can change that file gets them at the next logon.
data.comment: {0} is the path the logon task will start.

data.name: TaskInstalled
data.value: Installed the logon task {0}: it starts {1} at every logon.
data.comment: {0} is the task's name in Task Scheduler, {1} the path of the exe it starts.

data.name: TaskInstallFailed
data.value: Could not install the logon task: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, usually schtasks's exit code and what it printed.

data.name: TaskRemoved
data.value: Removed the logon task {0}.
data.comment: {0} is the task's name in Task Scheduler.

data.name: TaskWasNotInstalled
data.value: The logon task {0} was not installed, so there was nothing to remove.
data.comment: {0} is the task's name in Task Scheduler.

data.name: TaskRemoveFailed
data.value: Could not remove the logon task: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, usually schtasks's exit code and what it printed.

data.name: TaskInstalledStarts
data.value: The logon task {0} is installed; it starts {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the task's name in Task Scheduler, {1} the path of the exe it starts.

data.name: TaskInstalledUnknownExe
data.value: The logon task {0} is installed.
data.comment: {0} is the task's name in Task Scheduler. Used when the exe it starts couldn't be read.

data.name: TaskTrayMissing
data.value: Warning: {0} does not exist, so the logon task starts nothing. Reinstall Marquee, or run `marquee task install` from an administrator terminal.
data.comment: {0} is the path the logon task starts. The command stays as it is.

data.name: TaskNotInstalled
data.value: The logon task {0} is not installed. Run `marquee task install` from an administrator terminal to add it.
data.comment: {0} is the task's name in Task Scheduler. The command stays as it is.

data.name: TaskStatusFailed
data.value: Could not read the logon task: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, usually schtasks's exit code and what it printed.

data.name: TaskStarted
data.value: Started the logon task {0}: the tray is starting.
data.comment: {0} is the task's name in Task Scheduler.

data.name: TaskStartNoSession
data.value: {0} is not signed in, so the tray was not started now. It starts at their next logon.
data.comment: {0} is the user's security identifier (SID), such as S-1-5-21-…; it stays as it is.

data.name: TaskStartFailed
data.value: Could not start the logon task: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason, usually Task Scheduler's own text.

data.name: TraysStopped
data.value: Closed the trays running from {0}: {1} quit when asked, {2} had to be ended.
data.comment: {0} is the path of MarqueeTray.exe; {1} and {2} are numbers of running copies of it.

data.name: NoTrayRunning
data.value: No tray was running from {0}.
data.comment: {0} is the path of MarqueeTray.exe.

data.name: TrayStopFailed
data.value: Could not close the tray: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason (Windows' own text, already in the user's language).

data.name: UpdatesRemoved
data.value: Deleted {0} downloaded update files and the folder {1}.
data.comment: {0} is a number of files, {1} the folder they were in (%ProgramData%\Marquee\updates). Printed when Marquee is uninstalled.

data.name: UpdatesNotRemoved
data.value: Warning: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the reason the downloaded updates were not deleted, a sentence.

data.name: TaskFolderNotRemoved
data.value: Warning: could not delete the task folder {0}: {1}
data.comment: {0} is the logon task's folder in Task Scheduler (\Marquee), {1} Task Scheduler's reason (Windows' own text, already in the user's language).

data.name: DataFolderNotSecured
data.value: Warning: {0} Marquee is installed, but until then its tray won't start with administrator rights.
data.comment: {0} is why Marquee's folder in %ProgramData% isn't safe to use, sentences that end by saying how to fix it. Printed into the installer's log.

data.name: ClaimScreenNeedsAdministrator
data.value: `{0}` needs an administrator terminal, because stopping L-Connect's service takes administrator rights. Open Terminal or PowerShell with "Run as administrator" and run it again.
data.comment: {0} is the command, `marquee claim-screen`, which stays as it is. "L-Connect" is a program's name. "Run as administrator" is Windows' own menu item: use its name in the user's language.

data.name: ClaimScreenNoMarquee
data.value: No Marquee is running to take the screen. Start `marquee run` (or the tray) first, then run `marquee claim-screen` again.
data.comment: marquee claim-screen found no running Marquee, so it left L-Connect alone. The commands stay as they are.

data.name: ClaimScreenAlreadyHeld
data.value: Marquee already has the screen.
data.comment: marquee claim-screen found a running Marquee that has the screen already, so it left L-Connect alone.

data.name: EditElevated
data.value: This terminal is running as administrator, so marquee edit won't start the theme editor: the theme files it saved would belong to Administrators. Run marquee edit from a normal terminal.
data.comment: marquee edit, run as administrator, started nothing. The command name stays as it is.

data.name: EditorMissing
data.value: The theme editor isn't installed beside marquee.exe: there is no {0}. Reinstall Marquee to get it back.
data.comment: marquee edit found no theme editor. {0} is the full path of MarqueeEditor.exe where it looked.

data.name: EditorNotStarted
data.value: Couldn't start the theme editor: {0}
data.comment: marquee edit couldn't start MarqueeEditor.exe. {0} is the reason Windows gave.

data.name: EditStarted
data.value: Opened {0} in the theme editor.
data.comment: marquee edit started the theme editor. {0} is the theme's folder.

data.name: EditStartedConfigured
data.value: Opened the theme config.yaml names in the theme editor.
data.comment: marquee edit, with no theme given, started the theme editor on the theme config.yaml's theme: setting names, the one on the screen. config.yaml stays as it is.
